prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
System: Cedar Falls Municipal Drinking Water Treatment Plant control system. Mission: continuous potable water meeting regulatory, utility and demand targets. It gives operators visibility, automatic control and manual intervention points for intake, treatment, lab and distribution. Boundary: from River Intake Pump Station and Raw Water Screen Channel through treatment, disinfection and finished-water storage control to the High Service Pump Header.

Aliases:
- Ironwood = River Intake Pump Station. First controlled pumping, within approved withdrawal limits. Normally automatic; raw-water demand and channel depth govern pump starts.
- Lantern = SCADA Historian Server. Stores operating data for trends, compliance, incident reconstruction and performance.

Elements:
- Raw Water Screen Channel: monitored for upstream, downstream and differential level, rake run status and high-debris indications.
- Coagulant Dosing Skid: chemical feed per setpoints, raw-water conditions and operator direction.
- North and South Filter Gallery: parallel; show status, headloss, turbidity and backwash control.
- Chlorine Contact Basin: disinfection contact control point.
- Clearwell Level Controller: finished-water storage control point.
- Backwash Recovery Tank; Laboratory Sample Receiving Bench (receives process and compliance samples); instrumentation.

Actors:
- Chemical Supplier Driver: controlled delivery; inventory checked before setpoints change.
- Laboratory Technician: analytical confirmation; reports unusual results to operations.
- Chief Operator: authority over modes, production targets, treatment and abnormal response; authorizes Storm Intake Mode.
- Duty Engineer: configuration control; approves engineering changes.
- Maintenance Planner: turns equipment condition into planned work.
- Distribution Dispatcher: sends demand changes and delivery expectations to the plant.
- Residuals Hauler: removes residuals and backwash recovery material.
- North and South Distribution Pressure Station: interfaces that influence finished-water pumping.

Modes (intake): Automatic (normal); Reduced-capacity (low river level, equipment condition or low demand); Storm Intake Mode (rainfall, river rise, debris or runoff), entered when normal assumptions are unreliable; staff increase observation of river level, screen loading, turbidity and pump cycling.

Alarm: Chlorine Residual Alarm is high priority (public-health risk, analyzer fault or process issue); needs immediate operator assessment.

Requirements: all controllers, panels, workstations, analyzers and Lantern shall stay synchronized to plant time. Trained staff supervise automatic control, use safe manual operation and document deviations.

External interfaces: power, chemical delivery, lab information, residuals removal, distribution communications.

New part:
S033: A rising differential level across the Raw Water Screen Channel is treated as an early indication of screen blinding or heavy floating debris.
S034: The Raw Water Screen Channel sends the Rake Torque Snapshot at the end of each cleaning cycle to preserve the recorded loading condition.
S035: If the Raw Water Screen Channel shows rapid level change, plant staff verify that the cleaning mechanism is running and that the River Intake Pump Station is not drawing the channel down too quickly.
S036: A high-high level condition at the Raw Water Screen Channel requires immediate field confirmation because it may indicate restricted passage, failed cleaning, or abnormal river backwater.
S037: Raw-water quality triggers include high turbidity, unusual color, odor complaints from field staff, visible sheen, algae accumulation, and rapid temperature change.
S038: When a raw-water quality trigger occurs, the Chief Operator determines whether to adjust pumping rate, request additional laboratory testing, or increase downstream process monitoring.
S039: The Laboratory Technician supports intake decisions by prioritizing raw-water checks when storm runoff or an abnormal visual condition is reported.
S040: The Coagulant Dosing Skid is placed under closer observation when intake turbidity changes faster than the normal control response can stabilize.
S041: The North Filter Gallery and South Filter Gallery are advised when incoming water quality is expected to shorten filter run time or increase solids loading.
S042: Pump permissives at the River Intake Pump Station include adequate suction level, available discharge path, healthy motor status, open isolation valves, and absence of active protective trips.
S043: A pump is not permitted to start when the Raw Water Screen Channel downstream level is below the established low-level limit.
S044: A pump start is also blocked when the associated drive reports a fault, when local control is selected, or when a safety interlock is not proven.
S045: If a permissive is lost during operation, the control system either alarms the condition or stops the affected pump according to the severity of the signal.
S046: The Chief Operator may authorize temporary manual operation only when the cause is understood, the equipment can be observed, and the risk to treatment continuity is acceptable.
S047: The SCADA Historian Server retains river level, screen differential, pump status, and raw-water quality trends for operating review and event reconstruction.
S048: The Duty Engineer reviews storm forecasts and river-stage information when a prolonged debris event or high-flow period is expected.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
